transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-19 16:30 UTC | Duration ~48m | Attendees: Daniel Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Sparrow Head of Platform), Marcus Wu (Infra), Priya Patel (Product), Tommy (note taker)

Summary: Short discovery to validate fit for PLG/self-serve route, understand Sparrow's constraints around data residency and compliance, agree pilot scope (free credits, time-to-first-token goal), and schedule a technical deep dive for benchmark.

Topics: quickstart credits, TTFT (time-to-first-token), hosted vs dedicated vs private, VPC/on-prem constraints, SOC2/KMS/audit logs, performance benchmarks (latency vs cost), sample payloads for pilot, rollout plan and success criteria.

[00:00] Daniel Park: hey everyone, uh thanks for jumping on, i'm daniel from Redwood, i'm the AE on this — quick intros?
[00:12] Lena Ortiz: hi i'm lena, head of platform at Sparrow, we own infra + platform for the product teams, nice to meet you all.
[00:18] Marcus Wu: marcus here, infra, we'll be doing the bench and look at networking constraints.
[00:23] Priya Patel: priya product, i'll be owning success criteria from a product POV.
[00:28] Daniel Park: awesome, and maya is our solutions engineer, she'll walk through the quickstart and perf bits. maya?
[00:33] Maya Singh: hi! yeah thanks daniel. um quick agenda: 1) how you want to get to first inference (time-to-first-token), 2) what constraints you have (data residency, encryption), 3) pilot scope (free credits / sample bench) and 4) next steps. sound good?
[00:47] Lena Ortiz: sounds good, we're on a tight timeline — the product team wants a prototype in ~3 weeks, ideally we hit TTFT within 2 days for a small team.
[00:56] Daniel Park: okay that's helpful, 3 weeks to prototype is realistic. how many requests per second are you expecting at the start?
[01:03] Priya Patel: initial traffic low, maybe 5-10 rps from internal users, but we want to test a HF (high-frequency) path later, so we care about throughput too.
[01:12] Marcus Wu: i want to flag network / security: we'll need private networking (VPC peering) for the pilot if possible, and our security folks ask about KMS integration for keys and audit logs. SOC 2 is in flight.
[01:26] Maya Singh: yep we do VPC peering for Redwood Private and Dedicated; Hosted + private link options exist — also we integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping, and provide audit logs and token-level tracing in the console. could you share the specific KMS provider?
[01:40] Marcus Wu: we use Google KMS primarily, some teams use Hashi corp vault, not sure about HSM needs yet.
[01:48] Daniel Park: okay we'll note that. for the PLG path, most teams try self-serve hosted first using our free credits to validate models and latency. then if they need predictable throughput or VPC, they move to Dedicated or Private.
[02:01] Lena Ortiz: that's kind of our question — do we start hosted and move later or go direct to dedicated? cost vs latency tradeoff.
[02:07] Maya Singh: yep that tradeoff's common. hosted gives fastest TTFT and easiest onboarding — we'll give X credits (we'll detail amount in the playbook) and a quickstart repo to get you to a token in minutes. Dedicated gives lower variance for p95 latency and reserved capacity but requires procurement lead time. Private adds VPC and KMS control but more setup.
[02:29] Marcus Wu: procurement lead time is 4-6 weeks at Sparrow, so we can't block on that for the prototype. can hosted hit our security bar for a pilot?
[02:38] Maya Singh: depends on audit requirements. for low-sensitivity data you can use hosted with encrypted artifacts; for e2e encryption and full KMS control you'd likely pick Private. Also note: hosted can be configured with controlled retention and we can toggle minimal logging. we'll share a security packet.
[02:55] Priya Patel: product wants to evaluate quality too — can we test with our internal dataset? contains some PII (hashed), is that a problem?
[03:03] Daniel Park: hashed PII is generally fine for a functional pilot. we'll still need to validate retention policies with your compliance contact.
[03:10] Lena Ortiz: perfect. on performance — maya, can you explain how Redwood handles batching and kv cache — we've seen issues with models where long context makes latency unpredictable.
[03:20] Maya Singh: sure — our runtime supports continuous batching with workload-aware batching policies; we do KV cache reuse for chat-style workloads and prefix caching. that reduces per-token compute. for long context the kernel selection and quantization path matters — we'll suggest configs based on sample sequence length distribution.
[03:41] Marcus Wu: do you have an out-of-the-box quantized model that works well or do we need custom conversion?
[03:47] Maya Singh: we have pre-quantized variants for common open models, and we also advise on 4-bit/8-bit quantization tradeoffs. for the pilot we can start with a verified profile to keep dev friction low.
[03:58] Daniel Park: quick question — how quick is time-to-first-token for hosted typical?
[04:02] Maya Singh: for small models on hosted it's minutes from sign-up; for larger LLMs expect a few minutes for warm-up; we have streaming responses too so first bytes come fast. our goal for PLG quickstart is <30 minutes to first production-ish inference, but many teams hit in under an hour.
[04:19] Lena Ortiz: under an hour is okay for a prototype. we want to set an internal goal of <1 day.
[04:24] Priya Patel: any limits on prompt size during quickstart?
[04:27] Maya Singh: default limits are 4k tokens depending on model; we can increase in pilot.
[04:33] [05:00] (crosstalk) Tommy: note — request for end-to-end example repo link
[05:05] Daniel Park: yeah i'll send the quickstart repo and a small sample app.
[05:09] Lena Ortiz: on the cost side, can you share rough unit economics so we can model?
[05:14] Daniel Park: yes, i'll include a model/cost matrix in the pricing doc — it shows per-token cost for hosted and reserved pricing for Dedicated. we'll also show how batching/caching changes effective unit cost.
[05:25] Marcus Wu: for the perf benchmark — can we run a head-to-head at same sequence length on hosted and dedicated? we want p50/p95/p99 latencies.
[05:33] Maya Singh: yes, we'll run identical payloads and capture token-level latency. for dedicated we can provision reserved GPU pool for the bench so you see stable p95.
[05:43] Lena Ortiz: compliance question — is there support for SSO and RBAC for team access?
[05:46] Maya Singh: yes SSO via SAML/OIDC and RBAC scoped to routes and tokens, plus audit logs. we'll share the admin docs.
[05:55] Priya Patel: what about model versioning and rollouts — we might A/B test different prompts/models with users.
[06:01] Maya Singh: we support model pinning and rollout policies (canary/A-B) in the console; you can route by route or by header and fall back to a cheaper variant if higher-latency model fails.
[06:15] Marcus Wu: any gotchas w/ our infra — we run in multiple GCP regions, we need region affinity to reduce egress.
[06:22] Daniel Park: region routing is supported; you can pin to region or we can route to the nearest. we'll capture region preferences in the pilot config.
[06:30] Lena Ortiz: ok good. so pilot scope suggestion?
[06:33] Daniel Park: propose 3-week pilot: week 0 sign-up + quickstart (use free credits) get TTFT <1 day for basic flows; week 1 perf bench hosted vs dedicated with sample payloads; week 2 iterate on security controls and finalize go/no-go. credits will cover pilot compute.
[06:50] Priya Patel: that aligns with product timeline. what success metrics do you recommend?
[06:54] Maya Singh: recommend: functional parity (answers correct on N evaluation prompts), latency SLO p95 under X ms (we'll define), and cost per 1k tokens within budget. also operational: integration with your KMS and RBAC.
[07:10] Marcus Wu: about data residency — we might need EU-only residency for some datasets. is that supported on hosted?
[07:16] Maya Singh: we have regional hosting options in EU; for strict residency you'd pick dedicated or private in region. we'll note that in the security packet.
[07:26] Lena Ortiz: okay great. two quick technical asks: 1) can we get an example Traf flow for VPC peering and 2) a sample script to run the bench with redis for caching?
[07:37] Maya Singh: yes to both, we'll include a network diagram and bench script; maya will run an initial bench for you.
[07:44] Daniel Park: cool. any other blockers on your side?
[07:47] Priya Patel: procurement will need the pilot T&Cs for free credits, and legal will want the data flow diagram.
[07:54] Daniel Park: we'll include a one-pager T&C and a data flow diagram. i'll send both.
[07:59] Marcus Wu: on monitoring, do you expose per-route traces and token-level cost to our console?
[08:05] Maya Singh: yes per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdown and tracing hooks. you can also stream logs to a customer SIEM via our audit exporter.
[08:15] Lena Ortiz: can you confirm what we should send for sample payloads? anonymized logs or synthetic?
[08:20] Maya Singh: anonymized logs are preferred but synthetic is fine to start. we'll provide a template.
[08:27] [08:50] (silence for a few seconds)
[08:52] Daniel Park: ok wrap up — recap next steps: i'll send pricing + quickstart repo + security packet + pilot T&C. maya will run perf bench and share initial numbers. lena will provide compliance contact and confirm stakeholders. schedule technical deep dive next week.
[09:10] Priya Patel: sounds good, thanks.
[09:12] Lena Ortiz: thanks all.

Recap / Action items (verbatim):
- Daniel Park: Send pricing + pilot agreement + quickstart repo (includes sample app) — due 2026-05-22
- Maya Singh: Run dedicated vs hosted perf test with sample payloads and share p50/p95/p99 by 2026-05-25
- Lena Ortiz: Provide compliance contact and confirm pilot stakeholders by 2026-05-21

Questions (raised during call):
- Is hosted acceptable for initial pilot given Sparrow's compliance requirements? (answered: depends, we'll share security packet)
- Can we run head-to-head hosted vs dedicated for p95 stability? (answered: yes; SE will run bench)

References/links mentioned (to be sent): quickstart repo, pilot playbook, security packet (SOC2/KMS/audit logs), pricing matrix, bench script and network diagram.

Notes on transcription: some product names were misrecognized (e.g., "Kube-urn-eats" on one line instead of Kubernetes), occasional filler words, speaker overlaps.
